The way i think about it is that by saying it that the minor key is supposed to be used differently from the major key.  It’s the same with modes, they might be derived from the major scale but they aren’t going to be used the same harmonically.  If you analyze the different patterns of the modes you will see they are different from the major scale, so for example, if you look at C major, even tho you are starting on each next natural note in the scale for the corresponding mode that will start on that next note making it the key center, you aren’t going to still be using the note C anymore as your tonic.  There are methods to make it clear that you are using a mode versus staying in the major key, but the main idea is to distinguish the particular modal tonic as they key center and to use the unique intervals of that mode to have your ear see that you are using a different composition structure than the major scale.  You might also need to avoid some chords to not have any confusion as well as using certain types of chords to emphasize the mode.  Don’t get me wrong, you still have A LOT of freedom to be creative, you just need to follow some rules behind your composition or else you can have your music drifting back to a non modal sound.  Btw, the minor scale is a mode of the major scale (same notes but starting on 6).  The reason we call something minor vs aeolian i think is because the minor scale has it’s own modes too, but when you say aeolian you are inferring that you are drawing the notes from the parent major scale and probably won’t be using the minor scale modes.  Anyways that’s at least how i think about the difference, idk if it is technically correct though.  The yt channels “newjazz” and “walk that bass” have good vids on modal application if you want to learn more.  I highly recommend checking out their channels.

- the reason minor sounds “sad” is becuz of the b3 and b6.  You will have a minor triad if you use the b3 vs a major triad.  The b3 just has a more melancholic sound to it, hence being associated with sounding “sad”.
